MEMORANDUM
  Agenda Item #: 5
  Meeting Date: 10/13/2020

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL MEMBERS

THRU:  LAURA GUGLIELMO, CITY MANAGER

FROM:  BRIANNA RINDGE, ACTING PLANNING AND BUILDING
  DIRECTOR

SUBJECT:  RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE PARKLANDS COMMITTEE
  OF SEPTEMBER 10, 2020

DATE:  OCTOBER 13, 2020

ACTION REQUIRED  X  CONSENT  X  RECEIVE & FILE

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council approve the actions of the Parklands Committee
for the meeting of September 10, 2020.

Summary

In the Parklands Committee meeting of September 10, 2020, four committee members
were present for the first application and five members were present for the remaining five
applications. Two of the six applications requested tree removal or topping for view
purposes, two requested landscaping in Parklands or on a public path, and two requested
landscaping of a median. Last, the Ad Hoc committee for’ Landscape Design Standards
for Public Spaces’ provided an update.

Analysis and Findings

The City held a Parklands Committee meeting on September 10, 2020 and the Committee
recommended the following actions to be approved by the City Council.

1. PC-539-20; Application to landscape a portion of Parklands with native plants
  adjacent to 1400 Chelsea Road

Applicant: Jeff Jellison, 1400 Chelsea Road, Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

  1
 This hearing was continued from the previous Parklands Committee meeting to enable the
applicant to modify the plan according to the directions provided. The applicant reduced
the planting plan by 50% in density to improve access and eliminate any barrier to the
public and the submitted a design of a more random fashion along the perimeter adjacent
to the Parklands to reduce the appearance of a continuation of the adjacent private property.

Staff reviewed the general objectives of R12-05, the Parklands Landscaping Policy, which
are to keep the Parklands: open to the public; undeveloped and natural appearing; not a
barrier to the public; and not appearing privately owned. Staff indicated the following:

  1. Parklands adjacent to private property establishes a special circumstance which
  does not apply generally to other properties in the same area.
  2. Denial could create a hardship or practicable difficulty due to weed seeds in
  Parklands invading private property or weeds in Parklands reducing the value of
  the home.
  3. The addition of unusable native buffer landscaping to the property will not result in
  material damage or prejudice to other properties and will not be detrimental to
  public safety or welfare.
  4. The use of low density, randomly spaced native plants will not create a barrier to
  the public or, to the extent reasonably practicable, appear privately owned.

The applicant spoke at the meeting indicating access to the Parklands is provided, views
are protected and that any time a resident is willing to improve Parklands it should be
viewed as a benefit. Marlene Breen, the applicant’s project designer, indicated that the
new design meets all points of direction provided by the Parklands Committee and that the
project is at no cost to the City.

The majority of Committee members present agreed the plan addresses the concerns and
direction provided at the previous meeting and meets the four objectives of the Parklands
Landscaping Policy. Committee member Groves motioned, seconded by Committee
member Rhodes, to approve the application. The motion passed was 4-0 in favor, Cooper
absent.

The Parklands Landscaping Policy requires that a “legal contract between the City and the
property owner defining a maintenance schedule and standards that run with the property
in perpetuity is required.”

2. PC-540-20; Application to landscape the center median adjacent to City Hall with
  California friendly drought tolerant plants

Applicant: Palos Verdes Estates Foundation, PO Box 955, Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

This application to landscape the center median adjacent to City Hall was conceptually
approved at the previous meeting. Karen Logan presented a PowerPoint presentation that
highlighted the changes in the plant palette, noting the revised plan per directed by the
Committee, and indicated the project was now fully funded by donations.

  2
 During public comment, Marlene Breene supported the project generally but does not
support the revised plan. Ms. Breene indicated that the new plan appeared as two gardens
with clashing soft colors in one area and brassy colors in another area and that the boulders
should be placed in groupings in a more random fashion and recommended review by the
Palos Verdes Homes Association.

Chad McAllister of the Malaga Cove Homeowners Association (MCHA) indicated that
95% of Malaga Cove residents support the project and the MCHA is budgeted to provide
additional maintenance to ensure success.

The Foundation, not wanting any fiscal impact to the City, agreed to fund the boulder
harvesting and delivery with Bennett Landscaping.

One committee member requested clarification concerning the ‘Grow and Kill’
applications of herbicide. The committee agreed the median was not a place for children to
play and herbicide could be used, but requested yellow tape around the perimeter and use
of the least toxic type of herbicide.

Committee member Rhodes motioned and Committee member Cooper seconded to
recommend approval to the City Council and require the Palos Verdes Estates Foundation
to be responsible for the boulder harvesting and delivery, placing yellow tape around the
median during herbicide application, and that the herbicide shall be the least toxic type.
The motion passed unanimously (5-0).

3. PC-541-20; Application to landscape a portion of the path adjacent to 1733 Via
  Coronel with native ground cover

Applicant: Karl Fjoslies, 510 Agate Street, Redondo Beach, CA 90277

The applicant requests to install native grass in a portion of Lopez Path East. The grasses
are native to California and are sold under the name of ‘Native Mow Free’. The irrigation
for this portion adjacent to 1733 Via Coronel will be located on private property and no
sprinklers will be on the path.

Staff reviewed the general objectives of R12-05, the Parklands Landscaping Policy, which
are to keep the Parklands: open to the public; undeveloped and natural appearing; not a
barrier to the public; and not appearing privately owned. Staff indicated the following:

  1. Parklands adjacent to private property establishes a special circumstance which
  does not apply generally to other properties in the same area.
  2. Denial could create a hardship or practicable difficulty due to weed seeds in
  Parklands invading private property or weeds in Parklands reducing the value of
  the home.

  3
   3. The addition of unusable native buffer landscaping to the property will not result in
  material damage or prejudice to other properties and will not be detrimental to
  public safety or welfare.
  4. The use of low growing native grass in an un-cut and irrigated condition will not
  create a barrier to the public or, to the extent reasonably practicable, appear
  privately owned.

A few committee members disagreed with the project indicating it did not establish all four
factors. They indicated that more community outreach is necessary and that the applicant
shall contact all four properties adjacent to the path. The committee also stated that the
header board at the top of the path shall be removed and the applicant shall consider
landscaping the entire path. The item was continued.

4. PC-542-20; application to remove one Brazilian pepper tree located in the
  parkway adjacent to 2744 Via Campesina

Applicant: Marcie May, 2765 Via Campesina, Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced the item as a view application requesting removal of a Brazilian pepper
tree that obscures the view from the main viewing areas in the home. The tree has
penetrated the asphalt street and broken the curb. Staff noted the tree had been trimmed
recently without view improvement and safety of the street could not be repaired without
removing the tree.

The applicant expressed concern over the view blockage from the main viewing rooms in
the home. Amir Kaviani, the adjacent neighbor to the applicant, supported the application
and indicated it would also improve his view and address the safety issue of the curb and
street safety.

The Committee all agreed and were in favor of the application for two reasons: view
obstruction and street safety. Committee member Cooper motioned and Committee
member Rhodes seconded to recommend approval. The motion passed unanimously (5-0).

5. PC-543-20; application to top one Peruvian pepper tree located adjacent to 4415
  Via Azalea and three Peruvian peppers located adjacent to the Mirlo Gate Lodge
  Tower

Applicant: Brent Perekoppi, 4415 Via Azalea, Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this view application as a request to top the Peruvian pepper tree directly
behind their home and immediately above the stone entry sign on Via Valmonte and to top
three additional Peruvian pepper trees adjacent to the Mirlo Gate Lodge Tower by 5-10
feet each. Staff indicated the trees could be lowered by 5-10 feet but recommended a more
selective trimming to avoid arbitrary topping.

  4
 The applicant indicated he would like to restore the view he had when he moved in two
years ago and could see airplanes landing at Torrance Airport. He indicated he was not
interested in creating unattractive or hazardous trees and could work with the Urban
Forester to be more selective and prevent harming the trees.

Most of the Committee members agreed that topping was not appropriate but the trees
could be lowered with a more selective trimming. One committee member indicated the
trimming should be at the direction of the Urban Forester and there should exist a
maintenance agreement. One member asked if a reduction of 10 feet would restore the
view the applicant had in 2018. The applicant indicated it would be more than adequate.

Committee member Groves motioned to approve topping of the trees with no second.

Committee member Groves motioned and Committee member Rhodes seconded to
recommend approval to selectively trim the trees. The motion passed unanimously (5-0).

6. PC-544-20; Application to landscape the Lunada Bay fountain

Applicant: Lunada Bay Homeowners Association/Kristin Sweet, P. O. Box 51, Palos
Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Chair Richie-Bray, having reviewed and discussed the concept with the Lunada Bay
Homeowners Association, recused herself from this item to avoid a possible appearance of
a conflict of interest.

The application requests to restore the fountain’s perimeter planting and irrigation system
with a modified design of appropriate plants that maintains traffic and pedestrian safety
and adds colorful accent plants adjacent to the base of the fountain. A border of Palos
Verdes Stone is proposed around the perimeter edge adjacent to the asphalt street. All costs
are to be the responsibility of the Lunada Bay Homeowners Association.

The submitted plan was modified prior to the meeting to respond to the concerns expressed
in the staff report involving traffic safety and indicted this was to expedite approval for the
plan so the project could be completed prior to the holiday season. A new plan rendering
was not available for the meeting but the new conceptual plan retains all the low growing
juniper and adds colorful plants where sight lines for traffic safety are not affected.

The Committee expressed support of approving the landscape to enable the project to start
as soon as possible. Dwight Abbott of the Lunada Bay Homeowners Association supported
the plan and indicated that all safety concerns are addressed in the new plan.

During public comment, Marlene Breene suggested the City delineate the sight lines for
traffic safety and approve the plan to enable completion for the holidays and recommended
onsite direction.

  5
 The Palos Verdes Estates Foundation was in support of the project and indicated they will
be providing partial funding.

One Committee member expressed reluctancy to support without a new plan but the other
members were in full support of approval. Committee member Rhodes motioned and
Committee member Cooper seconded to recommend approval of the modified conceptual
plan. The motion passed 4-0 (Richie-Bray recused).

Adjourned at 9:20 p.m.

Notification

These matters have been agenized and posted in the routine manner.

Staff reported prepared by:
Carl Moritz, ISA Certified Arborist WE3939
Urban Forester
